overlap_rationale: Two recurring, role-conditioned skills are used, not separate color-specific policies. Let A_r/A_b denote acquire-and-lift red/blue and P_r/P_b denote carry-place-clear red/blue. The per-trajectory order is A_r -> P_r -> A_b -> P_b. All ranges are half-open action ranges with both endpoint observations inspected; no actions are excluded, including initial holds and final settling/retreat. Shared action ranges, in trajectory order demo10200 through demo10211, are A_r/P_r: [80,180), [75,170), [80,178), [78,176), [77,174), [79,177), [81,179), [84,184), [82,182), [76,175), [80,180), [78,173); P_r/A_b: [235,430), [225,410), [234,422), [232,420), [230,418), [233,421), [236,424), [242,434), [240,430), [231,419), [238,426), [229,417); A_b/P_b: [440,540), [425,525), [438,538), [436,536), [434,532), [437,535), [440,540), [450,550), [446,548), [435,533), [442,542), [433,531). Thus pickup/transport overlaps are 95-102 actions (4.75-5.10 s) and inter-object overlaps are 185-195 actions (9.25-9.75 s), not short boundary tails. Pickup overlaps begin during open-finger final descent and span closure, contact dwell, the entire vertical lift and early lateral transport. Inter-object overlaps begin with red still held and descending above its pad, include placement, opening, settling, vertical retreat, horizontal return and blue approach. Their endpoints have open fingers and TCP world z between about 0.055 and 0.222 m; the next pickup is still evolving. Acquisition of blue therefore supports takeover before red release, during opening, during retreat, or during blue approach, rather than only at one pregrasp pose. Carry/place likewise supports takeover before closure, during closure/lift, or after lift. The red carry segments end before blue closure, preserving a coherent place-and-clear core; subsequent closure and lift are shared by blue acquisition and blue carry. Boundaries were accepted individually from inspected states, not scaled from trajectory length: e.g. demo10201 at 425 is an open blue approach at z=0.089 m whereas demo10210 at 442 is at z=0.021 m; both precede closure, and each overlap includes a complete ensuing lift. No triple overlap or same-skill self-overlap is used. Longer overlap establishes temporal/contact-phase coverage along successful paths only, not recovery from off-path spatial/contact errors. During training use original trajectory/time identifiers to avoid accidental cross-segment stitching, distinguish role tags, and avoid counting duplicate overlap examples twice within a candidate's same training batch if windows coincide. Evaluate splits at whole-trajectory level rather than putting shared windows into different splits. These designs are hypotheses, not evaluated policies.
